title: NSW Digital Trade Licences (DTLs) – Terms and Conditions
summary: This page outlines the terms and conditions for using Digital Trade Licences (DTLs), which are electronic versions of physical contractor, supervisor, or tradesperson licences.
who_can_apply: Have or be able to obtain a MyServiceNSW Account.
Have or will link your MyServiceNSW Account to your Trade Licence.
what_you_need: A working electronic device with a charged battery and an unobstructed screen.

internal_links.text: Privacy Statement for Digital Trade Licences and Credentials

faqs.q: What is a Digital Trade Licence (DTL)?
faqs.a: A DTL is an electronic version of a physical contractor licence, supervisor certificate, or tradesperson certificate under the Home Building Act 1989. It can be used to show that you hold a current Trade Licence.

faqs.q: Must I always carry my physical Trade Licence?
faqs.a: Yes, because NSW is the first jurisdiction to offer a DTL, you should always carry your physical Trade Licence when working outside of NSW, as the DTL may not be recognised in other jurisdictions.

faqs.q: What happens if my phone or device is damaged?
faqs.a: You must ensure your phone or other electronic device is working, sufficiently charged, and that the screen is not cracked, dimmed, or obstructed, otherwise your DTL may not be accepted.
